pathway.title: Everforth Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The balance sheet, not the business, is the weak link. Total debt rose from 2.24x to 4.66x EBITDA and EBITDA cover of cash interest fell from 7.48x to 4.15x between FY2023 and the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, because principal debt grew while calculated EBITDA fell from USD 464.4 million to USD 299.6 million; the issuer prints no EBITDA, so both ratios use operating income plus amortization and depreciation. Net debt of USD 1,248.5 million is 4.17x EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C13

Earnings are eroding at the Commercial Segment, where about 70% of revenues sit. Revenue is 10.42% below FY2023 and EBITDA 35.49% below, and the issuer attributes 2026 gross margin compression to fewer permanent placements, a currency effect at its Mexican delivery centre and growth in lower-margin cloud work, while selling and administrative cost rose on strategy, outsourcing and acquisition integration. About 87% of Commercial revenue is time-and-materials and many client agreements may be terminated at will, so a demand fall reaches earnings quickly. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

Liquidity and refinancing rest on the revolver. Cash plus revolver availability of USD 374.5 million is 69.22% of the USD 541.0 million of notes due in 2028, and availability of USD 227.0 million is 54.60% below the USD 500.0 million of FY2024 because borrowings rose. The July 2026 amendment moved the revolver to 2031-07-07 and removed its 2028 maturity, so the first large maturity is the 2028 notes, followed by term loan B in 2030. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2024-12-31_efor-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02

Cash conversion is adequate but weakening. Free cash flow of USD 195.6 million over the last twelve months is 0.65 times EBITDA because capital spending is low, but nine-month operating cash flow fell to USD 129.4 million from USD 225.6 million on higher receivable days and lower cash earnings before working capital. Buybacks and acquisitions from FY2024 to the first nine months of 2026 exceeded free cash flow by USD 380.8 million, which is why net debt rose by USD 382.8 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C09

Federal backlog supports revenue but offers less cushion than its size suggests. Backlog of USD 2,943.4 million is 2.5 times revenue on contracts of three to five years, yet only 21.68% is funded, awards fell 9.44% over the last twelve months and book-to-bill is 0.9 times, so the segment is stable rather than growing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04

Financial policy is the swing factor. There is no sponsor and no dividend, but the company spent USD 547.8 million on buybacks and USD 587.7 million on acquisitions since FY2024 and USD 922.5 million of repurchase authority remains; the covenant maximum falls to 3.50x from the quarter ending 2027-06-30 and to 3.25x from the quarter ending 2028-06-30, so a resumption of buybacks while leverage is high would be creditor-adverse. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C09

runs.text: The credit's strongest supports are cash generation that stays positive on low capital spending, a federal book of work with multi-year contracts, and a revolver now extended to 2031-07-07 beside fixed-rate notes. Free cash flow of USD 195.6 million over the last twelve months is 0.65 times EBITDA because cash paid for property and equipment is about 1% of revenue, which means earnings convert into cash available for interest and repayment. Federal backlog of USD 2,943.4 million on contracts of three to five years means about 30% of revenues have visibility beyond the quarter, although only 21.68% of backlog is funded. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C04

The weaknesses are leverage, earnings erosion and refinancing. Total debt to EBITDA of 4.66x against 2.24x at FY2023, with cover of 4.15x against 7.48x, means interest absorbs a larger share of a smaller earnings base; calculated EBITDA is 35.49% below FY2023 on revenue 10.42% lower, which signals operating deleverage in a labour-based cost model; and cash plus availability of USD 374.5 million is below the USD 541.0 million of 2028 notes, so repayment depends on refinancing or on cash generation that has weakened in 2026. A fourth weakness is capital allocation: debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions raised principal debt by USD 350.2 million, and USD 922.5 million of repurchase authority remains. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C06

cells.text: Everforth, Inc., a Delaware corporation; the annual report states ASGN was incorporated in 1992; named ASGN Incorporated until 2026-04-24; principal office in Glen Allen, Virginia
New York Stock Exchange, ticker EFOR (ASGN before the rename); 41.1 million shares outstanding at 2026-10-23; 27 holders of record at 2026-02-12

IT solutions to commercial and government clients across six solution areas: cloud and infrastructure, data and AI, software development and engineering, customer experience, cybersecurity, enterprise platforms
Apex Systems, Creative Circle, CyberCoders, ECS, GlideFast and TopBloc; Quinnox joined the Commercial Segment in March 2026
Commercial (70% of 2025 revenues) and Federal Government (30% of 2025 revenues)
No client other than the U.S. federal government exceeded 10% of 2025 revenues; direct federal prime contracts were 26% of 2025 revenues
Virtually all revenues in the United States; foreign subsidiaries about 2% of revenues and 6% of costs of services in 9M 2026; two near-shore delivery centres in Mexico and one in India
About 19,600 billable professionals on a full-time-equivalent basis and about 2,800 internal employees in 2025
Commercial: 87% time-and-materials in 9M 2026, the rest fixed price; Federal: time-and-materials, cost reimbursable and firm-fixed-price, contracts of three to five years
Deloitte & Touche LLP; opinions on FY2024 and FY2025 statements state they present fairly, in all material respects; internal control attested at 2025-12-31
Senior secured credit facility: USD 600.0 million revolver due 2031-07-07 (373.0 drawn) and term loan B due 2030 (485.0); unsecured 4.625% senior notes due 2028 (541.0)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Everforth has made two acquisitions in the window, both for cash and both in the Commercial Segment, and has issued no new notes. TopBloc, a Workday consultancy, closed on 2025-03-04 for USD 340.0 million, 90% in cash and 10% in equity; Quinnox, a digital solutions provider, was announced on 2026-01-20 and closed in March 2026 for USD 290.0 million in cash. No sponsor, buyer or seller of the company is named, and the filings describe no leveraged buyout, recapitalisation or dividend. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_efor-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39

The debt changes were amendments, not new issues. A July 2025 amendment added a USD 100.0 million incremental term loan A, and a July 2026 amendment raised the revolver from USD 500.0 million to USD 600.0 million, moved its maturity from 2028-02-14 to 2031-07-07, repaid and terminated term loan A with revolver proceeds, and lowered the senior secured leverage maximum to 3.50x and 3.25x from the quarters ending 2027-06-30 and 2028-06-30. The unsecured notes changed only through an August 2026 open-market repurchase of USD 9.0 million principal at a USD 0.2 million discount, which left USD 541.0 million outstanding; the notes are dated in 2028 by year only, and their indenture is dated 2019-11-22. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-06-30_efor-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7

The company also approved a repurchase program of USD 1.0 billion on 2025-11-17, cancelling earlier authorisations; USD 972.0 million was available at 2025-12-31 and USD 922.5 million at 2026-09-30. The equity portion of TopBloc was paid with 0.5 million shares valued at USD 28.7 million, against 10% of the price of USD 34.0 million, a difference of USD 5.3 million that the filings do not explain. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_efor-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source readiness for Everforth Inc (formerly ASGN Incorporated), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the five supplied SEC filings (two annual reports and three quarterly reports) can support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit modules, and what stays unsupported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document date shown for each filing is the signature date printed in it; no filing date is stated in the filings themselves, and the FY2025 annual report gives 2025-02-24 as the filing date of the FY2024 annual report. No external source and no earlier analysis was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied filings support a financial, business and fundamental-credit view of Everforth Inc through the quarter ended 30 September 2026, but not verification of guarantees, covenant definitions or ratings, so those points stay as the filings describe them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The set is two annual reports and three quarterly reports from one registrant, known as ASGN Incorporated until 24 April 2026 and filed under one file number throughout. The newest report was signed 20 days before the as-of date of 2026-11-18, and nothing later was supplied, so any announcement since is not established. The credit agreement, note indenture, guarantor list, ratings, market prices and peer data are not in the set, and the issuer prints no adjusted EBITDA, so earnings measures must be built from the statements.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: The executed credit agreement, the note indenture, the list of subsidiaries and any guarantor schedule are not in the supplied set. The filings say only that the credit facility is secured by substantially all of the company's assets and list an indenture whose guarantors are not named. Who guarantees the debt, what is pledged, and how the senior secured and unsecured claims rank structurally cannot be established beyond those descriptions. The executed documents and the subsidiaries exhibit would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The lender-defined EBITDA used in the covenant and the secured debt counted against it are not supplied; the issuer states only the ratio, 2.12x at 2026-09-30 against a 3.75x maximum that steps down to 3.50x from the quarter ending 2027-06-30 and 3.25x from the quarter ending 2028-06-30. The five filings print no issuer EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so any earnings measure is built from operating income and amortization and depreciation. Headroom in earnings or cash terms cannot be recomputed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: Liquidity and maturity detail is thin. Revolver availability is stated as an approximate figure, letters of credit are stated only at 2025-12-31 (USD 3.7 million undrawn), and the stated availability at 2026-06-30 is USD 2.0 million below the revolver size less borrowings with no explanation. Term loan B and the notes are dated by year only. Each limits liquidity and maturity-ladder precision rather than the direction of any conclusion.

fields.value: - Minor: Periods and presentations are not fully comparable. No 2025 quarter-end balance sheet is supplied, so same-quarter leverage comparisons for 2025 cannot be built; the fourth quarter of 2025 is derived, not reported. Commercial revenue is split into consulting and assignment in the 2025 annual report but by five industries in the 2026 reports, which give only an approximate consulting share. Federal customer-type revenue for 2024 was recast between the two annual reports, the FY2025 report aggregates balance-sheet lines the FY2024 report shows separately, and Quinnox goodwill moved between the first and later 2026 reports because purchase accounting is provisional.

fields.value: Total debt at carrying value rose from USD 1,041.6 million at FY2023 to USD 1,396.0 million at 2026-09-30, while EBITDA calculated from the statements fell from USD 464.4 million to USD 299.6 million over the last twelve months, so total debt to EBITDA moved from 2.24x to 4.66x. Revenue fell from USD 4,450.6 million in FY2023 to USD 3,980.4 million in FY2025 and has been flat since, at USD 3,986.8 million over the last twelve months, while the calculated EBITDA margin dropped from 10.43% to 7.51% as gross margin narrowed and selling and administrative cost rose. The debt was added to buy growth and return capital rather than to fund operations: acquisitions of USD 587.7 million (TopBloc in 2025, Quinnox in 2026) and buybacks of USD 547.8 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 754.7 million by USD 380.8 million between FY2024 and the first nine months of 2026, and net debt rose USD 382.8 million. Creditors therefore hold more claims against a smaller earnings base. The one structural improvement is the revolver, which the July 2026 amendment enlarged and extended, but the drawn amount has grown so that availability of USD 227.0 million is well below the USD 500.0 million of FY2024.

fields.value: Cash generation weakened faster than earnings in 2026. Operating cash flow was USD 129.4 million in the nine months against USD 225.6 million a year earlier, partly because working capital absorbed USD 49.5 million (a release of USD 7.7 million a year earlier), driven by receivables of USD 92.5 million which the issuer attributes to more days sales outstanding, and partly because cash earnings before working capital fell to USD 178.9 million from USD 217.9 million. Last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 195.6 million is still about two-thirds of EBITDA after capital spending of USD 36.1 million, and no dividends are paid, so the working-capital outflow can reverse; if it does not, cash conversion rather than earnings becomes the binding constraint on repaying the revolver.

fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is USD 374.5 million, cash of USD 147.5 million plus about USD 227.0 million available under the USD 600.0 million revolver, of which USD 373.0 million is drawn. The July 2026 amendment moved the revolver maturity from 2028-02-14 to 2031-07-07, repaid term loan A with revolver draws and removed the 2028 revolver maturity, so only USD 5.0 million of principal falls due within 12 months. The maturity wall is therefore the 2028 notes (USD 541.0 million, plus a small term loan instalment) and then the 2030 term loan B remainder (USD 468.75 million). Neither falls due within 12 months, but cash plus availability of USD 374.5 million is below the USD 541.0 million of notes, so repaying them depends on a refinancing or on cash generation, and because liquidity is mostly the revolver, any draw raises leverage one for one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's own covenant ratio looks comfortable but cannot be tested. Senior secured debt to lender-defined consolidated EBITDA was 2.12x at 2026-09-30 against a 3.75x maximum that falls to 3.50x from the quarter ending 2027-06-30 and 3.25x from the quarter ending 2028-06-30. The ratio has risen from 1.09x at 2024-12-31 and 1.49x at 2025-12-31 to 2.13x, 2.17x and 2.12x at the three 2026 quarter-ends, so on the issuer's own figures the gap to the maximum is 1.63x today and would be 1.38x and 1.13x at the two step-downs if the ratio stayed at 2.12x; that is a gap between two stated ratios, not a measure of EBITDA or debt capacity, which cannot be inferred. The same secured principal over the EBITDA calculated here is 2.86x, so the lender definition adds back or nets roughly 0.74x of leverage that the filings do not itemize. The direction matters more than the level: the ratio nearly doubled in under two years and the step-downs narrow the allowance even if earnings stabilise. The FY2024 annual report applies the test when the revolver is drawn and the later reports omit that condition; the revolver is drawn at 2026-09-30, so the test applies on either wording.

The July 2026 amendment and the August 2026 repurchase of USD 9.0 million of notes at a USD 0.2 million discount are inside the third quarter. No event after 2026-09-30 is stated, so the post-balance-sheet table carries none; the earlier acquisition and financing events are already in the interim net debt rows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that the balance sheet is not stretched on the issuer's own measures: covenant leverage is 2.12x against 3.75x, the revolver was upsized and extended to 2031, the fixed coupon on the 2028 notes is below the 5.3% weighted-average cash interest rate, federal backlog is USD 2,943.4 million at 2.5 times revenue, and no shares were repurchased in the third quarter and no dividends are paid, although USD 922.5 million of the repurchase authorization remains. Acquisition, integration and strategic planning costs of USD 30.9 million in the nine months (USD 15.8 million a year earlier) also depress calculated EBITDA, and an adjusted measure could add them back, but the filings state no adjusted EBITDA and do not say whether the lender definition does so. That view wins if EBITDA stabilises near USD 300 million, receivables days normalise and net debt falls; it loses if the quarterly EBITDA decline continues (third quarter EBITDA USD 85.5 million against USD 97.2 million) or the revolver draw rises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A supported downside sequence starts with weaker Commercial demand and slower federal awards: commercial consulting book-to-bill was 0.9 times in the third quarter and federal book-to-bill 0.9 times over the last twelve months. Falling gross margin (28.27% in the third quarter against 29.36% a year earlier) and receivable days would then cut EBITDA and operating cash flow, forcing revolver draws to cover interest and buybacks, which lifts leverage and, with the covenant step-downs from mid-2027, narrows the allowance. Observable triggers are quarterly EBITDA below the third-quarter level, availability below USD 227.0 million and any resumption of buybacks while net debt exceeds 4x EBITDA. No numerical stress or cash runway is established here.

fields.value: The document date shown for each filing is the signature date printed in it; the filings state no filing date. No external source was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Everforth is a publicly held IT consulting and staffing group with no sponsor or controlling holder named, so creditors depend on management's own capital allocation, which has funded acquisitions and buybacks with debt while earnings fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: From FY2024 to the first nine months of 2026 the company repurchased USD 547.8 million of stock and paid USD 587.7 million for two acquisitions, while principal debt rose USD 350.2 million to USD 1,399.0 million and operating income fell from USD 364.1 million in FY2023 to USD 230.3 million in FY2025. The company has never paid a dividend, buybacks stopped in the third quarter of 2026 and the July 2026 amendment lowered the covenant maximum from mid-2027, but USD 922.5 million of repurchase authority remains and the proxy statement that would show owners, board independence and pay is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk rests on management's capital allocation, not on an owner: no sponsor, fund or controlling holder is named, the company had 27 holders of record in February 2026 plus beneficial owners through brokers, and the board chair is separate from the chief executive. Because the proxy statement is not supplied, ownership above reporting thresholds, board independence and executive pay are not established, so the assessment reads behaviour only and settles on a Medium risk level that rests on behaviour alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 81; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns and acquisitions were funded partly with debt while earnings fell, which is the main creditor-adverse behaviour in the record. Buybacks of USD 547.8 million and two acquisitions costing USD 587.7 million between FY2024 and the first nine months of 2026 compare with principal debt up USD 350.2 million, and the share count fell about 12% from the end of 2023 to October 2026, so cash that could have repaid debt went in part to shareholders. This reading is an analyst interpretation of the cash flow and debt tables, because the filings do not name the funding source of each use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_efor-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2024-12-31_efor-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C04; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is moving toward consulting but is not yet earning more. Commercial consulting grew to 32.41% of FY2025 revenues from 24.61% in FY2023 as assignment work fell from 46.71% to 37.69%, yet Commercial segment operating income fell from USD 344.1 million in FY2023 to USD 248.1 million in FY2025 and by a further 23.32% in the first nine months of 2026. The issuer attributes the 2026 gross margin compression to fewer permanent placements, a weaker currency effect at the Mexican delivery centre and faster growth in lower-margin cloud services, and selling and administrative cost rose on acquisition, integration and strategic planning cost of USD 30.9 million against USD 15.8 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C01; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Commercial revenue visibility is short-cycle. About 87% of Commercial revenues in 2026 come from time-and-materials contracts, and the annual report states that many client agreements are not exclusive and may be terminated at will, so revenue depends on continued client orders rather than contracted backlog; the 70% revenue weight of this segment therefore carries most of the earnings risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Federal Government segment gives steadier but shrinking visibility. It is 30% of revenues on contracts of three to five years with backlog of USD 2,943.4 million, 2.5 times revenue, but awards over the last twelve months fell 9.44% to USD 1,049.2 million, book-to-bill is 0.9 times, backlog is 4.64% below a year earlier, and cost-reimbursable contracts rose to 34.25% of nine-month segment revenue from 30.52%, which carry lower margin. Direct federal prime contracts were 26% of 2025 revenues and the annual report names budget delays, a government shutdown and efficiency efforts as causes of lower 2025 revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C02; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The July 2026 amendment extended maturities and tightened the covenant but also enlarged secured borrowing capacity. The revolver rose from USD 500.0 million to USD 600.0 million and its maturity moved from 2028-02-14 to 2031-07-07, term loan A was repaid and terminated, and the senior secured leverage maximum falls from 3.75x to 3.50x from the quarter ending 2027-06-30 and to 3.25x from the quarter ending 2028-06-30, against an issuer-stated ratio of 2.12x. The facility is secured by substantially all assets and the notes are unsecured and subordinate, but guarantors, collateral terms and the covenant definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring of results but not of creditor control. Audited annual statements, an auditor's report on internal control and quarterly reports are filed, and the company states it complied with its covenants at each reporting date from 2024-12-31 to 2026-09-30, yet no adjusted EBITDA, compliance certificate, covenant definition or guarantor list is supplied, so a creditor monitors the issuer's single stated covenant ratio rather than headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium risk reading is that management has already moved toward creditors in 2026. Buybacks stopped in the third quarter after small purchases in the second, the company accepted lower covenant maximums from mid-2027, repurchased USD 9.0 million of its notes below par, has never paid a dividend, and the stated covenant ratio of 2.12x sits well inside the 3.75x maximum. Federal backlog of USD 2,943.4 million also supports cash flow even as Commercial earnings weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three things would move the risk level to High: a resumption of repurchases while leverage is rising, a further debt-funded acquisition, or a proxy statement showing a controlling holder or related-party payments. A sustained halt to repurchases, falling debt and disclosure of guarantor and covenant terms showing that distributions are restricted would move it to Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement, executed credit agreement and note indenture are not supplied, so ownership concentration, board independence, restricted-payment capacity and guarantor scope are not established; this keeps the governance risk level at Medium on behaviour evidence and means the capacity to resume buybacks cannot be tested against the debt documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Purchase accounting for Quinnox is provisional for 12 months from closing and the 2026 reports describe Commercial revenue by industry rather than as consulting and assignment, so the consulting share after 2025 is not established and the consulting-led margin conclusion rests on 2025 and earlier data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment results are shown without segment cash flow or customer detail beyond the federal customer types, so customer concentration below the 10% threshold and segment cash conversion are not established; revenue durability is read from contract types and backlog only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The newest evidence is signed 2026-10-29 and nothing later is supplied, so events in the 20 days to the as-of date are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Everforth has made two acquisitions in the window, both for cash and both in the Commercial Segment, and has issued no new notes. TopBloc, a Workday consultancy, closed on 2025-03-04 for USD 340.0 million, 90% in cash and 10% in equity; Quinnox, a digital solutions provider, was announced on 2026-01-20 and closed in March 2026 for USD 290.0 million in cash. No sponsor, buyer or seller of the company is named, and the filings describe no leveraged buyout, recapitalisation or dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt changes were amendments, not new issues. A July 2025 amendment added a USD 100.0 million incremental term loan A, and a July 2026 amendment raised the revolver from USD 500.0 million to USD 600.0 million, moved its maturity from 2028-02-14 to 2031-07-07, repaid and terminated term loan A with revolver proceeds, and lowered the senior secured leverage maximum to 3.50x and 3.25x from the quarters ending 2027-06-30 and 2028-06-30. The unsecured notes changed only through an August 2026 open-market repurchase of USD 9.0 million principal at a USD 0.2 million discount, which left USD 541.0 million outstanding; the notes are dated in 2028 by year only, and their indenture is dated 2019-11-22.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company also approved a repurchase program of USD 1.0 billion on 2025-11-17, cancelling earlier authorisations; USD 972.0 million was available at 2025-12-31 and USD 922.5 million at 2026-09-30. The equity portion of TopBloc was paid with 0.5 million shares valued at USD 28.7 million, against 10% of the price of USD 34.0 million, a difference of USD 5.3 million that the filings do not explain.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_efor-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions while earnings fell, because cash went to shareholders and sellers instead of debt repayment, which implies higher leverage and refinancing reliance. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any dividend, the pause in buybacks and the lower covenant maxima.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Everforth presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions while earnings fell, which matters because the cash went to shareholders and sellers rather than to debt repayment and implies higher leverage and more reliance on the revolver and refinancing. Countervailing evidence is that the company has never paid a dividend, stopped repurchases in the third quarter of 2026 and agreed lower covenant maxima. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and the guarantor list. The governance and sponsor assessment is completed with limitations, with a Sponsor / Governance Risk Level of Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Everforth Inc (formerly ASGN Incorporated) as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the five supplied filings through the quarter ended 2026-09-30 and the supplied analyses of source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance; no rating, market price, peer data or executed legal document is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document date shown for each filing is the signature date printed in it; the filings state no filing date. No external source was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Everforth's credit quality is weakening: total debt reached 4.66x EBITDA from 2.24x at FY2023 as debt funded buybacks and acquisitions while earnings fell, so creditors depend on cash conversion recovering and on refinancing the 2028 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business itself is adequate, with revenue of USD 3,986.8 million over the last twelve months, a federal backlog of USD 2,943.4 million and positive free cash flow of USD 195.6 million. But liquidity of USD 374.5 million is mostly the revolver and is smaller than the USD 541.0 million of notes due in 2028, EBITDA covered cash interest only 4.15x against 7.48x in FY2023, and the issuer's covenant ratio of 2.12x against a 3.75x maximum cannot be tested. The primary downside path is weaker Commercial earnings feeding revolver draws before the 2028 maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C01; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The balance sheet, not the business, is the weak link. Total debt rose from 2.24x to 4.66x EBITDA and EBITDA cover of cash interest fell from 7.48x to 4.15x between FY2023 and the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, because principal debt grew while calculated EBITDA fell from USD 464.4 million to USD 299.6 million; the issuer prints no EBITDA, so both ratios use operating income plus amortization and depreciation. Net debt of USD 1,248.5 million is 4.17x EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are eroding at the Commercial Segment, where about 70% of revenues sit. Revenue is 10.42% below FY2023 and EBITDA 35.49% below, and the issuer attributes 2026 gross margin compression to fewer permanent placements, a currency effect at its Mexican delivery centre and growth in lower-margin cloud work, while selling and administrative cost rose on strategy, outsourcing and acquisition integration. About 87% of Commercial revenue is time-and-materials and many client agreements may be terminated at will, so a demand fall reaches earnings quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and refinancing rest on the revolver. Cash plus revolver availability of USD 374.5 million is 69.22% of the USD 541.0 million of notes due in 2028, and availability of USD 227.0 million is 54.60% below the USD 500.0 million of FY2024 because borrowings rose. The July 2026 amendment moved the revolver to 2031-07-07 and removed its 2028 maturity, so the first large maturity is the 2028 notes, followed by term loan B in 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2024-12-31_efor-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is adequate but weakening. Free cash flow of USD 195.6 million over the last twelve months is 0.65 times EBITDA because capital spending is low, but nine-month operating cash flow fell to USD 129.4 million from USD 225.6 million on higher receivable days and lower cash earnings before working capital. Buybacks and acquisitions from FY2024 to the first nine months of 2026 exceeded free cash flow by USD 380.8 million, which is why net debt rose by USD 382.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Federal backlog supports revenue but offers less cushion than its size suggests. Backlog of USD 2,943.4 million is 2.5 times revenue on contracts of three to five years, yet only 21.68% is funded, awards fell 9.44% over the last twelve months and book-to-bill is 0.9 times, so the segment is stable rather than growing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor. There is no sponsor and no dividend, but the company spent USD 547.8 million on buybacks and USD 587.7 million on acquisitions since FY2024 and USD 922.5 million of repurchase authority remains; the covenant maximum falls to 3.50x from the quarter ending 2027-06-30 and to 3.25x from the quarter ending 2028-06-30, so a resumption of buybacks while leverage is high would be creditor-adverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weakening view is that the issuer's own measures are not stretched: its covenant ratio is 2.12x against a 3.75x maximum, the revolver now runs to 2031-07-07, the 2028 notes carry a fixed coupon below the 5.3% average cash rate, free cash flow stays positive and buybacks stopped in the third quarter. These facts do not prove headroom, because the ratio is on lender-defined EBITDA and secured debt that are not supplied, and the same secured principal over EBITDA calculated here is 2.86x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if quarterly EBITDA held above the third-quarter level of USD 85.5 million, receivable days normalised, net debt fell and the 2028 notes were refinanced early. It would worsen if quarterly EBITDA kept falling, revolver availability fell below USD 227.0 million, or repurchases resumed before leverage fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is calculated from operating income and amortization and depreciation because the issuer states none, so the leverage and cover conclusions are house measures that cannot be compared with covenant or agency ratios; the amortization line also exceeds itemized components by a small amount that moves FY2025 leverage by 0.11x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lender-defined EBITDA, covenant definitions and the compliance certificate are not supplied, so the covenant ratio of 2.12x cannot be converted into headroom and no capacity to fund buybacks or acquisitions is inferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, market price, peer set or executed legal document is supplied, so market access, relative value, structural priority and recovery are not assessed and the refinancing conclusion rests on maturity timing and liquidity alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The analysis is backward-looking: there is no forecast, no 2025 quarter-end balance sheet and no segment cash flow, so the downside path is qualitative and its one sensitivity is arithmetic on trailing figures, not a projection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit's strongest supports are cash generation that stays positive on low capital spending, a federal book of work with multi-year contracts, and a revolver now extended to 2031-07-07 beside fixed-rate notes. Free cash flow of USD 195.6 million over the last twelve months is 0.65 times EBITDA because cash paid for property and equipment is about 1% of revenue, which means earnings convert into cash available for interest and repayment. Federal backlog of USD 2,943.4 million on contracts of three to five years means about 30% of revenues have visibility beyond the quarter, although only 21.68% of backlog is funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_efor-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_efor-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weaknesses are leverage, earnings erosion and refinancing. Total debt to EBITDA of 4.66x against 2.24x at FY2023, with cover of 4.15x against 7.48x, means interest absorbs a larger share of a smaller earnings base; calculated EBITDA is 35.49% below FY2023 on revenue 10.42% lower, which signals operating deleverage in a labour-based cost model; and cash plus availability of USD 374.5 million is below the USD 541.0 million of 2028 notes, so repayment depends on refinancing or on cash generation that has weakened in 2026. A fourth weakness is capital allocation: debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions raised principal debt by USD 350.2 million, and USD 922.5 million of repurchase authority remains.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Everforth, known as ASGN Incorporated until 2026-04-24, sells IT consulting, staffing and digital engineering through two segments: Commercial, about 70% of revenues, serving large corporate clients mainly under time-and-materials contracts, and Federal Government, about 30%, serving defense, intelligence, national security and civilian agencies on contracts of three to five years. Consulting is 62% of 2025 revenues, no client other than the federal government exceeded 10% of 2025 revenues, and virtually all revenues arise in the United States. The staffing heritage gives a labour cost that flexes with hours worked and a talent pool shared by short and long contracts, which supports cost flexibility, but the same structure means most Commercial revenue is short-cycle and can be terminated at will, so cash-flow visibility comes from the federal backlog and from client renewals rather than from contracted revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is publicly held on the New York Stock Exchange with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named, 27 holders of record in February 2026 and a share count that fell about 12% from the end of 2023 through repurchases. Governance evidence is limited to the annual report: the chair is separate from the chief executive, ten directors signed, and Delaware takeover provisions make an unsolicited change of control harder; ownership above reporting thresholds, board independence and pay sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The group is the parent and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, consolidated; the senior secured facility is secured by substantially all assets and the 2028 notes are unsecured and subordinate with guarantors that are not named, so structural priority below the facility cannot be mapped. The business and governance analysis assigns a Medium sponsor and governance risk level, driven by debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions while earnings fell, and this analysis adopts it.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is volume-driven by billable hours and headcount at rates set by competitive bidding and client negotiation, with little contractual protection: about 87% of Commercial revenue is time-and-materials, many agreements are non-exclusive and terminable at will, and the issuer cites a lower mix of permanent placement revenue and a shift toward lower-margin cloud services as 2026 margin drags. Consulting grew 14.35% in FY2025 while assignment fell 13.81%, which management presents as a move to higher-margin work, but Commercial segment operating income fell 23.32% in the first nine months of 2026, so pricing power is not evident. Federal revenue is steadier but flat: contracts last three to five years, backlog is USD 2,943.4 million and 2.5 times revenue, yet awards trail revenue (book-to-bill 0.9 times) and government budget delays, continuing resolutions and a shutdown reduced 2025 revenue. Revenue is therefore cyclical and discretionary in Commercial, budget-dependent in Federal, and not structurally declining but flat after a decline of 10.42% from FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of services is mainly compensation of contract professionals, so gross margin of 28.0% moves with rates and utilisation, while selling and administrative cost, which rose to USD 668.3 million in the first nine months of 2026 from USD 643.5 million, is largely fixed in the short run; with revenue 10.42% below FY2023, EBITDA margin fell 2.92 percentage points to 7.51%, which is the operating deleverage a creditor should expect to repeat in a volume decline. The company is spending to change its cost base, through back-office outsourcing to a single vendor, an enterprise resource planning system and strategy work, with acquisition, integration and strategic planning cost of USD 30.9 million in nine months against USD 15.8 million a year earlier, but the savings are not quantified. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through hiring and utilisation, but the 2026 record shows them eroding under adverse mix and integration cost, so margin resilience is limited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low, with cash paid for property and equipment of USD 36.1 million over the last twelve months, so free cash flow was USD 195.6 million, 0.65 times EBITDA, after cash interest of USD 72.2 million. Conversion is weakening because receivable days sales outstanding rose, absorbing USD 49.5 million of working capital in nine months against a release of USD 7.7 million a year earlier, and because cash earnings before working capital fell to USD 178.9 million from USD 217.9 million; the issuer describes first-quarter operating cash flow as seasonally low. Outside debt, non-cancelable purchase obligations were USD 217.2 million at 2025-12-31, with USD 81.3 million due in 2026 and USD 52.0 million in 2027, and operating lease liabilities were USD 64.0 million, so fixed cash calls compete with debt service; capital spending can be cut but is already small, so it is not a large source of flexibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: the annual report describes an industry that is highly competitive and fragmented with limited barriers to entry, which caps pricing on assignment work and means a loss of share shows up first in Commercial gross margin. The threat of new entrants is similar for the same reason, so margin cannot rely on barriers. Substitutes matter through artificial intelligence, which the company is both using and investing in; as an analyst inference it could substitute for lower-end engineering and staffing hours, a risk to assignment revenue that is already falling, while the company's own data and AI offerings are a potential support. Buyer power is strong because clients can place orders with competitors and terminate at will, and the federal government awards work by competitive bidding. Supplier power sits with the skilled workforce and a single outsourcing vendor: wage inflation or a vendor failure would raise cost of services or disrupt back-office processing, which feeds directly into margin and receivable collection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three factors alter credit quality. Federal spending priorities, continuing resolutions and shutdowns delay awards and funding, and the company states that its 2025 revenue fell partly because of efforts by the Department of Government Efficiency, tariffs and a shutdown, so policy moves federal revenue and the backlog's funding; the company also names rising interest rates among the causes. The economic cycle matters because demand for IT consulting is discretionary and because USD 858.0 million of debt floats, so a 100 bp rise costs about USD 8.6 million a year or 11.91% of last-twelve-months cash interest. Technology change, including artificial intelligence, shifts the mix of work and is both a revenue opportunity and a substitution risk. Social factors are not a primary credit driver on the supplied evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: federal backlog on multi-year contracts; low capital spending and positive free cash flow; revolver extended to 2031-07-07 with a covenant that steps down, which the company accepted; fixed-rate notes that cap a share of interest cost; no dividend. Weaknesses: total debt to EBITDA of 4.66x and cover of 4.15x; earnings erosion in Commercial; liquidity that is mostly the revolver and smaller than the 2028 notes; weak disclosure for covenant and guarantee analysis. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: faster growth in higher-margin consulting, realised savings from outsourcing and systems spending, and repayment of the revolver from free cash flow if buybacks stay paused. Threats that could weaken it: federal budget delays, an AI-driven fall in assignment demand, further debt-funded acquisitions or buybacks, and a refinancing of the 2028 notes in a weaker earnings position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale (revenue of USD 3,986.8 million), low capital spending, positive free cash flow and a federal backlog on multi-year contracts. The main constraints are total debt to EBITDA of 4.66x, margin erosion in Commercial, liquidity that is smaller than the 2028 notes, and a financial policy that has favoured buybacks and acquisitions over debt reduction. The trend is down on leverage (2.24x to 4.66x), on cover (7.48x to 4.15x) and on EBITDA margin (10.43% to 7.51%), and flat on revenue. Margin stability and financial policy are the weakest areas on the 2026 record, refinancing capacity depends on the 2028 notes, and free cash flow stability and liquidity are middling: positive and low-capex, but falling in conversion and mostly revolver. The key missing datapoints are the covenant definitions, guarantor and collateral terms, any rating or market pricing for the notes, and a company forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the outlook is flat revenue with pressured earnings: nine-month revenue is up only 0.21% and quarterly EBITDA fell to USD 85.5 million from USD 97.2 million, while the covenant maximum steps down to 3.50x from the quarter ending 2027-06-30 and the 2028 notes approach. Tailwinds are the consulting mix shift, federal National Security growth, the extended revolver and savings from outsourcing if they arrive; headwinds are Commercial margin compression, falling federal awards, rising receivable days, a seasonally weak first quarter and fixed purchase obligations. Over three to five years the outcome depends on whether consulting growth lifts segment margins and whether the 2028 notes and the 2030 term loan B are refinanced at similar cost; the sector headwind is artificial intelligence substitution and the sector tailwind is client demand for cloud, data and cybersecurity work, which management names as key areas of technological advancement. The filings do not give a company forecast, so these are directional views.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with a Commercial demand shock that the filings show is already under way: consulting book-to-bill was 0.9 times in the third quarter, clients can terminate at will, and federal awards are below revenue. The first operating break is lower utilisation and rates in time-and-materials work, which cuts gross margin below 28.27% while the selling and administrative base stays fixed. Financial transmission is lower EBITDA and slower collection, so operating cash flow falls further than earnings, as it did in 2026, and the revolver absorbs the gap together with fixed purchase obligations; revolver availability of USD 227.0 million is already 54.60% below the USD 500.0 million available at FY2024. As an arithmetic illustration only, a 10% fall in trailing EBITDA with debt and interest unchanged would lift total debt to EBITDA to 5.18x and cut cover to 3.73x. The leverage and refinancing consequence is that the covenant maximum steps down to 3.50x from the quarter ending 2027-06-30, the secured lenders' allowance narrows while the 2028 notes approach with liquidity of USD 374.5 million against USD 541.0 million. Management levers are paused buybacks, lower capital spending and savings from outsourcing, and these appear sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a moderate shock but not to repay the notes without refinancing. Observable triggers are quarterly EBITDA below USD 85.5 million, revolver availability below USD 227.0 million, a book-to-bill ratio below 1.0 in both segments and any resumption of repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Everforth presents an adequate business profile supported by federal backlog, low capital intensity and positive free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by total debt to EBITDA of 4.66x, falling earnings in the Commercial Segment and liquidity that is smaller than the 2028 notes. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but weakening because working capital and lower cash earnings cut nine-month operating cash flow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings stabilising near USD 299.6 million, on the revolver staying available to 2031-07-07 and on the market for the 2028 notes, for which no rating or price is supplied. The primary downside path is weaker Commercial earnings feeding revolver draws and debt-funded shareholder returns ahead of the 2028 maturity and the lower covenant maxima. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, covenant definitions and compliance certificate, the proxy statement, and any rating or market pricing. The fundamental credit analysis is completed with limitations. Top Risk: refinancing the 2028 notes after Commercial earnings erode further.
